citations.authors: W. Thies

reception: Reception came chiefly from the design-automation community for microfluidic biochips. There the paper's mixing algorithm, rather than its layered architecture, is the working object: a line of sample-preparation papers — on layout-aware, efficient, robust, and multi-target mixture preparation and dilution — takes it as the baseline method to improve upon, while others build dilution algorithms on its ideas or use it inside larger flows such as assay locking against bio-IP theft. The abstraction-layer argument itself surfaces mainly in passing mentions and survey citations, so in the citing literature the paper functions less as a programming-systems proposal than as the reference dilution algorithm.
